findings.body: The function is documented to shorten text to "at most `limit` characters", and the module doc says it is used for check-run titles because GitHub imposes a ceiling. In the `None` branch — when the first `limit` characters contain no space — the function returns `head` (which is exactly `limit` chars) plus `…`, for a total of `limit + 1` characters. If a caller passes GitHub's title ceiling as `limit` and the title has no space in that span, the result exceeds the ceiling the function exists to enforce. The `Some` branch is correct (it yields at most `limit` chars including the ellipsis); only the no-space path overflows.
findings.title: shorten can return limit+1 chars, exceeding the cap it enforces

value.summary: The new `summarise::shorten` can return `limit + 1` characters in its no-space branch, contradicting its documented contract of "at most `limit` characters" — a problem if the caller passes GitHub's title ceiling as the limit. The `first_sentence` function and the MongoDB kernel-bypass shim look sound. The compose/env-var rename depends on `server::auth::AppAuth::from_env` reading the new names, which I could not verify from the diff.
